evidence_items.locator: section Only the tip of the iceberg, paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: The study shows a clear increase over time in the number of electronic health record entries mentioning AI chatbot use with potentially harmful consequences.

evidence_items.explanation: A study of records from about 54,000 psychiatric patients, covering up to June 2025, found a clear rise over time in documented harmful chatbot use. Worsened delusions were the main harm.

evidence_items.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (Dow Jones Newswires)

receipt.public_excerpt: In the past nine months, these experts have seen or reviewed the files of dozens of patients who exhibited symptoms following prolonged, delusion-filled conversations with the AI tools.

evidence_items.explanation: Leading psychiatrists report dozens of new delusion cases tied to chatbot use in the nine months before late December 2025. That supports a growing problem shortly before the post.

evidence_items.locator: section Only the tip of the iceberg, paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Part of the increase we observe is probably due to greater awareness of the technology among the healthcare staff writing the clinical notes.

evidence_items.explanation: The lead author warns that part of the rise reflects greater awareness. This limits how much of the rise is true growth, but he still calls the problem under-detected.

unresolved_gaps: No population-level incidence data on chatbot-linked delusions exist. The trend comes from documented cases.
Kashmir Hill's NYT case counts are paywalled and were not checked directly.
